races.name: UB40 Ali Campbell At Chepstow Racecourse 24th July Handicap

runners_data.name: Notable Charm
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type with poor recent form (0-9-6), a fade tendency in finishes, and only one career placing in three runs on similar going — Ashley Lewis on a 0/1 trainer-14-day return makes this a very tough ask.

runners_data.name: Madame Passant
runners_data.note: Nicola Currie partners this hold-up filly whose last three efforts are all deeply unimpressive, and her record of two finishes from three on Good ground offers little encouragement at this longer 1m2f trip.

runners_data.name: Us Officer
runners_data.note: Tom Dascombe's three-year-old has shown some ability (a 4th, a 6th) but is a genuine hold-up horse operating out of role here — with five hold-up types in the field, securing a clear run late on a flat track against a likely uncontested leader is a significant ask.

runners_data.name: Hello Garda
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race, handled by apprentice Finlay Bassett, who has zero wins from 14 starts in 14 days for the trainer — the fade flag and modest form string (8-004) are real concerns, but uncontested lead on flat ground in Good to Firm is a major structural asset.

runners_data.name: Summer Oasis
runners_data.note: Mark Usher's filly has one win from seven in the past 14 days and her form figures of 0-8-9-0-8 suggest she has not translated her preferred hold-up style into any real threat — shunted toward midfield on the map but her natural place is at the back of this field.

runners_data.name: No Drama Mama
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's operation has produced two wins from 21 in 14 days, and this filly carries her natural closer's style into a race where five similar types are competing for the same ground late — her best form came at 6f on Soft, raising a query over 1m2f on Good to Firm.

runners_data.name: A Daughters Love
runners_data.note: Two placed efforts from nine runs on Good going (3rd twice over 10f) give this David Flood filly the most relevant course-profile evidence in the field — she is a true hold-up horse placed into midfield on the map, but her 10f form on Good is a genuine positive distinguisher.

runners_data.name: Lady Lauren
runners_data.note: Ed de Giles' three-year-old has placed twice (2nd and 3rd) on Soft and Firm ground at 8f but drops to OR 46 after a 10-place effort over 12f on Soft last time — the step back in trip helps, though she too will be fighting for a clear run from the hold-up pack.

races.paceDynamic: Hello Garda is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with no genuine rival to push them off the front, they are set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m2f trip on Good to Firm ground at Chepstow. That uncontested lead on a flat track in decent going creates a classic soft-fractions scenario where the leader's sectionals are never truly tested, making it very difficult for hold-up horses to generate the finishing momentum needed to reel them in. The remainder of the field — Us Officer, Summer Oasis, No Drama Mama, A Daughters Love and Lady Lauren — are all natural hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map because this race simply cannot accommodate that many closers at the rear; the true prominent berths behind Hello Garda are likely to be taken by whichever of those horses' riders elect to push forward from the gate. This shape strongly favours Hello Garda to control proceedings and any runner compact enough in their positioning to track just off the pace, as the lack of genuine pace pressure means the winner is most likely to come from on or near the front.

watchPoints.text: Hello Garda leads from the front completely unchallenged — if Finlay Bassett is allowed to bowl along in isolation, the rest of the field may simply never get close enough to challenge in the straight.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up types (Us Officer, Summer Oasis, No Drama Mama, A Daughters Love, Lady Lauren) all want the same late ground — watch for a traffic jam in the straight if they are all produced together without a clear gap.

A Daughters Love's two third-place finishes over 10f on Good going make her the most form-relevant threat if she can find daylight late — Jack Doughty will need to balance position against the fade flag noted in her profile.

Summer Oasis and No Drama Mama both have trainer 14-day form to consider (1/7 and 2/21 respectively) — Summer Oasis's trainer is live with runners while Hello Garda's trainer posts 0/14, which is a meaningful contextual signal.

The entire field is winless 3-year-olds with fade tendencies flagged on multiple runners — if Hello Garda ties up badly in the final furlong, the race could dissolve into a scramble between tired horses rather than a clean late surge.

races.name: Hayleys Race To Happily Ever After Restricted Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Pageant Girl
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Good going last time out (her most recent form string's standout result) and races prominently under Ashley Lewis (5lb claimer); the step back to a similar trip and surface she has already excelled on is a clear angle, and James Owen's 11/47 14-day strike rate is modest but not alarming at 55 days since last run.

runners_data.name: Super Tuscan
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner for Eve Johnson Houghton who has only seen Firm and Good-to-Firm ground; stepping from 5f to 6f is an unknown, and with zero wins or places from two runs she needs the pace duel to fully materialise to deliver a late run that counts.

runners_data.name: Dream On Kent
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner wearing a visor for David Evans, who ran 2nd over 7f on Soft last time before finishing 8th over 6f on Good — the drop back to Good to Firm and likely pace battle with Invicta Rose raises stamina and settlement questions; Ryan Kavanagh (5lb) rides.

runners_data.name: Invicta Rose
runners_data.note: Another confirmed front-runner for Ollie Sangster under Nicola Currie, who finished 4th over 6f on Soft last time; racing on faster ground today (Good to Firm) over the same trip suits and she has the class rating to cope with the pace duel if she can lead rather than fight for it.

runners_data.name: Miss Moneypit
runners_data.note: Unproven running style for Rod Millman; three runs all over 5f with finishes of 5-4-8 suggest limited improvement on this step up to 6f, and on faster ground than her best effort (4th on Good) she is hard to place confidently in any scenario.

runners_data.name: Curious Minx
runners_data.note: Lightly raced Richard Hannon runner — just one start (7th over 5f on Good) — whose inexperience makes the step to 6f a genuine unknown; the yard's 5/62 14-day record shows decent volume and Hannon can place unexposed types, but this is a significant leap on minimal evidence.

runners_data.name: Em's Dilemma
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who finished last (11th) over 7f on Soft on debut and carries an explicit fade flag; David Evans runs her alongside stablemate Dream On Kent, and without meaningful improvement from that dismal introduction she is very difficult to support in any pace shape.

runners_data.name: Lushill
runners_data.note: Quick 4-day turnaround for J S Moore (0/15 in 14 days, no recent winners), who was 5th over 6f on Good on debut — the trainer's cold recent form and very short recovery period temper expectations, though the previous run over the same trip and going is at least directly relevant experience.

races.paceDynamic: Invicta Rose and Dream On Kent are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the first stride over this 6f Good to Firm Chepstow trip, creating a genuinely contested early pace rather than a soft, dawdling gallop. With both horses rated OR=120 and racing off 14-day breaks, neither is likely to yield willingly, meaning the fractions will be honest to brisk from the outset. Pageant Girl will look to track closely in a prominent pitch, while the hold-up horses — Super Tuscan and Em's Dilemma — are reliant on that contested pace to set up a late run, though Em's Dilemma carries a notable fade flag. The contested early battle between the two front-runners burns energy from the pace-setters and stretches the field, which on fast Chepstow ground with its stiff finish marginally favours horses who race prominently but with cover — the prominent-to-midfield profile — over pure hold-up types who need a true test that may not fully materialise in a sprint-distance novice.

watchPoints.text: If Invicta Rose and Dream On Kent lock horns immediately from the gates, watch whether one capitulates before halfway — if neither gives ground, both may stop sharply inside the final furlong and hand the race to Pageant Girl tracking just behind.

Em's Dilemma is flagged as a horse who fades in the finish and finished last on debut — with Tyler Heard in the saddle, monitor whether she is pulled up or eased if she drops away quickly, which could affect surrounding runners in a tight 8-runner field.

Lushill's 4-day turnaround with a trainer showing 0 wins from 15 runners in 14 days is a significant concern — watch the market to see whether she is supported despite the quick return or drifts, indicating connections are simply taking a run.

Curious Minx (Richard Hannon) is completely unexposed after one run; watch for market activity from the Hannon yard as a guide to whether there is stable confidence in ability that the form book cannot yet reveal.

Good to Firm ground (confirmed in the going report despite the declared going showing Good) will be faster than several of these have encountered — watch specifically Super Tuscan, who has raced on Firm before, and Dream On Kent, whose only Good-ground run produced an 8th, to see if they handle the quicker conditions in the paddock.

races.name: Bell Cleaning Handicap

runners_data.name: Hallandale Beach
runners_data.note: Unrated style uncertain (U) but recent form on Good and Standard over 5-6f is consistent with a placed effort here; Kevin Philippart De Foy stable is 1/14 in 14 days and Rowan Scott is a competent booking — at OR 63 this 3yo rates a live each-way player if it can secure a tracking position and handles the step up in pace class.

runners_data.name: Who Is Alice
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse by style, returning after 36 days off with William Carson in the plate — its best form came on Soft/Yielding (2nd at OR equivalent on Soft) and the Good To Firm here may not be ideal; sim-going record of 6/10 with 1W2P suggests it can handle it, but the hold-up style in a slow-run race is a tactical disadvantage.

runners_data.name: Ahead Of Fashion
runners_data.note: A hold-up performer whose last five starts are all at 7f — dropping to 6f is a genuine query, and on Good To Firm this may be sharper than it has seen; the 5lb claim for Ffrench Davis is useful ballast but the stable's 1/9 in 14 days is modest and all historical form has come at longer trips.

runners_data.name: Corniche Girl
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type in reality, though shown in midfield on the map to reflect redistribution — all five recent runs have produced placed efforts at 6-8f on Standard/Good, but the style mismatch in a slow-run race with Ken Brulee dictating from the front makes a late run difficult to execute against a stacked hold-up field.

runners_data.name: Luna Beaux
runners_data.note: Adrian Wintle's hold-up filly shows one win on Standard at 6f and a clutch of fourth-place finishes; placed in midfield on the map but her natural position is off the pace, and with STYLE_FIT of 0.92 she is working against the race shape — the 5lb claim for Langley may compensate marginally but the scenario needs to suit.

runners_data.name: Pimentel
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and back after a 166-day absence — its best form is at 7f on Good (won) and Good to Soft (placed), so both the shorter trip and the fast ground are untested concerns; Marcus Tregoning sends it out without a 14-day strike rate (0/3) and the hold-up style in this shape is the least-favoured position, though raw ability on day one back could flatter.

runners_data.name: Ken Brulee
runners_data.note: The race's de facto pace-setter, though naturally a prominent-to-hold-up type pushed to the lead on the map — wore a visor last time, won at 6f on Good, and returns just 9 days after its last start; STYLE_FIT of 0.80 reflects it racing slightly out of role, but with no other confirmed early pace in the race it has every chance to dictate a sustainable tempo and prove hard to peg back.

races.paceDynamic: Ken Brulee is the only confirmed pace-setter in this 7-runner 6f handicap at Chepstow, redistributed to the front having shown prominent tendencies, and on Good To Firm ground he is likely to bowl along at a sustainable but uncontested gallop with no genuine front-runner to press him. Corniche Girl, Pimentel, and Luna Beaux are all true hold-up types pushed into a midfield mapping because the field is too hold-up-heavy to accommodate them all at the back — in reality they will trail the field and require a strong late move. Who Is Alice and Ahead Of Fashion are also natural hold-up horses, meaning this race features a lone pace-setter flanked almost entirely by horses that want to come from behind, which will likely produce a steady to honest gallop rather than a true-run test. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can absorb at the rear — Ken Brulee is best positioned to actually secure its role, with Hallandale Beach and Who Is Alice most likely to track closest in behind. On a flat, galloping track like Chepstow with an uncontested lead and a predominantly hold-up field, the race shape strongly favours any horse that can race prominently and maintain momentum into the final furlong without being challenged early.

Pimentel's 166-day layoff — Marcus Tregoning runners returning from a long absence at 0/3 in 14 days is a caution flag, and any ring rustiness from this horse means it could detach off the back in a 7-runner field with no cover to run into.

With five genuine hold-up horses in a 7-runner field, watch the draw and early positioning — any horse that drifts wide seeking a clear run risks giving away lengths it cannot recover in a race likely to be run at a controlled tempo off a lone, uncontested leader.

races.name: Paving Fields Construction Maiden Handicap

runners_data.name: Thai Princess
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding-trained hold-up filly returning after 61 days; has form at 7f on standard going and her three career runs all came at this trip, which is encouraging, though the long layoff and need for a strong pace to deliver her best are worth noting.

runners_data.name: Imagine That
runners_data.note: Henry Candy runner with a recent 15-day turnaround; finished fifth twice on good ground at 6f but her natural racing style is at the back, and with so many rivals seeking a similar position she will likely find herself further forward than suits — her sim-going record reads 1W from 4 runs on comparable ground.

runners_data.name: Mister McGregor
runners_data.note: Experienced four-year-old who has placed twice at 7f and wears an eye-shield; a natural rear-of-field type who in this congested hold-up field may be unable to secure his preferred pitch, and his recent form — including a 14th on good ground — does little to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Havana's Dream
runners_data.note: Ronald Harris runner stepping back from 8f to 7f, a trip where she posted a fifth last time; races with a phood-hood, is a genuine hold-up performer who finds herself in a race where the back of the field is overcrowded, and her good-going figures (5 from 12 on comparable surface) suggest no major ground concern.

runners_data.name: Creciente
runners_data.note: Rod Millman three-year-old with an 8 from 9 strike-rate on good going in terms of placing in the frame, yet still without a win; carries only 120lbs as one of the lightest in the race and races with a phood-hood, though her natural come-from-behind instincts will be compressed into a midfield slot she doesn't truly want.

runners_data.name: Jackabi
runners_data.note: Ian Williams gelding at OR 65, the highest-rated runner; has finished second twice at 7f on standard going and wears hood and tongue-tie — his form trajectory from 2-2 at the trip and the class edge over most rivals makes him the most credible rival to Okiru in a shape where a prominent stalker can land a blow, though his jockey is a 5lb claimer.

runners_data.name: Okiru
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's three-year-old is the lone front-runner and maps to control this race; the blinkers are on, he is fresh off a seven-day turnaround, and his prominent style in a field of hold-up types means he can dictate pace and fractions — the style-fit tag is a mild temper on confidence given he has never won, but structurally he holds the best position in this race shape.

races.paceDynamic: Okiru is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner maiden handicap over Chepstow's flat seven furlongs on good-to-firm ground, and with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, William Cox can dictate a controlled, even gallop from the outset. The field is unusually loaded with hold-up types — Imagine That, Creciente, Mister McGregor, Havana's Dream, and Creciente are all natural come-from-behind horses, but with so many genuine hold-up runners, most will find themselves shuffled into a bunched midfield rather than achieving their preferred position at the back. Thai Princess and Jackabi carry the most credible form from behind, but neither is a natural closer who thrives when a leader dictates a modest tempo unchallenged. This race shape — one lone leader controlling an uncontested, sustainable pace on fast ground — squarely favours horses who can travel prominently or make a smooth mid-race move, and any runner capable of sitting just off Okiru's shoulder and kicking entering the final two furlongs holds a structural advantage over those needing a strong pace to pounce from deep.

watchPoints.text: Okiru (William Cox) — if he jumps cleanly and is allowed to stride into an uncontested lead within the first furlong, he may prove very difficult to catch given the rest of the field is made up of hold-up types unable to apply early pressure.

Jackabi (Ryan Kavanagh, 5lb claimer) — at the highest OR in the race he is the most likely to hunt Okiru down from a stalking position, but a 5lb apprentice on a horse that has never won introduces execution risk at a crucial stage.

Imagine That, Mister McGregor, Havana's Dream, and Creciente — all four are genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield; watch for a congested early position as all four seek the back of a seven-runner field simultaneously, which could cause interference or hamper their runs.

Thai Princess (Callum Hutchinson) — 61 days off the track is the longest layoff in the field; watch how she moves to post and whether she travels fluently early, as ring-rustiness in a race lacking genuine pace could strand her further back than she needs to be.

Going conditions — declared as Good To Firm across all Chepstow races today despite the card header listing Good; fast ground suits Okiru's front-running style and may inconvenience horses like Havana's Dream and Mister McGregor who have winning or placing form on softer surfaces.

races.name: DragonBet Welsh Racing Festival 9th-11th October Handicap

runners_data.name: Act Of Violence
runners_data.note: Last ran 156 days ago which is a significant absence flag, but David Loughnane has a reasonable recent strike rate (2/12 over 14 days) and this horse has competitive form at 6f on similar going; a genuine hold-up operator who needs others to generate pace — in a no-pace race that is a concern, though its 5f record on good ground (8/15 sim-going) shows reasonable course exposure.

runners_data.name: Secret Handsheikh
runners_data.note: Ran just 5 days ago so fitness is assured, and Joe Leavy takes the ride for the in-form John Gallagher yard (1/6 T14); the visor is worn and this veteran 8-year-old has consistent recent form at 5f and 6f on good ground, though its sim-going record (0W2P) suggests placed rather than winning — will need the race to pan out perfectly.

runners_data.name: Dragon God
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll sends this 4-year-old out fresh (23 days), and its recent placed efforts at 5f and 6f on good ground (0W2P in sim-going) suggest competitive without winning; naturally a hold-up horse pushed into a midfield slot in the visualisation because the field has no genuine pace, meaning it could find itself in an unfamiliar forward berth with a STYLE_FIT of 0.90 tempering expectations.

runners_data.name: Some Nightmare
runners_data.note: The blinkers are on for this 9-year-old, and William Carson is an experienced pilot who could manufacture a position in a no-pace race; its sim-going record stands at just 2/15 (1W1P) which is modest, and while its hold-up style is genuine, the redistribution to midfield in the map reflects a crowded rear guard — STYLE_FIT 0.91 suggests limited upside if it cannot get its natural run.

runners_data.name: Macarone
runners_data.note: Grace Harris's 5-year-old runs off a 14-day break with apprentice Ben Ffrench Davis (5) claiming the allowance, but the form figures (094087) are difficult to excuse and its sim-going record on good-to-firm conditions is 0W0P from two attempts — a true hold-up type shuffled into midfield in the visualisation, and the STYLE_FIT penalty (0.92) combined with poor recent form make this one hard to back.

runners_data.name: Captain Bentley
runners_data.note: A notable 236-day layoff is the dominant flag here, and the warning tag of fading in the finish compounds concern for a horse asked to produce a late burst off such a long absence; Captain Bentley's recent form reads 86000- and its natural hold-up style is redistributed to midfield in the visualisation, with STYLE_FIT 0.91 suggesting it will struggle to deliver even if it gets into a good position.

races.paceDynamic: This is a six-runner 5f handicap at Chepstow on Good to Firm ground with no confirmed front-runner in the field — every single runner carries a hold-up profile, meaning the race will almost certainly unfold as a slowly-assembled sprint with horses tracking alongside each other before a mass cavalry charge to the line. Without a genuine pace-setter to force the tempo, the early stages are likely to be cautious and tactical, with the field compressing quickly and the race effectively becoming a flat-out dash from around halfway. In a race devoid of natural leaders, the winner will almost certainly come from whoever can quicken sharpest off a moderate gallop, favouring the horse with the best turn of foot and the most recent fitness edge rather than any positional advantage. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can comfortably place, with Dragon God, Some Nightmare, Macarone, and Captain Bentley all redistributed to midfield in the visualisation — in practice, one or two will be forced to take a slightly more forward position than is natural, but none are genuine front-runners and none will control the race; the tactical verdict is clear: with no pace, this race strongly favours a horse that can produce a sharp, sustained late burst from a handy position over a short 5f trip on fast ground.

watchPoints.text: Act Of Violence and Secret Handsheikh are the two runners with the most coherent recent form at the right trip and going — watch whether either can manufacture a handy position in a race where all six are trying to sit in.
Captain Bentley returns from 236 days off with a fade-in-finish flag and modest form — monitor in-running for any signs of being outpaced early, as it has little margin for error at this OR.

Dragon God, Some Nightmare, and Macarone are all genuine hold-up types pushed forward in the visualisation because no true pace horse exists — watch the early stages closely to see which of the six blinks first and takes up a forward role, as that horse could steal the race if the tempo never truly develops.

The going is officially Good to Firm for this 5f race despite the declared Good — the fast surface will sharpen the sprint finish and reduce the time available for closers to produce a sustained run, favouring any horse that can break alertly and maintain rhythm throughout.

races.name: Reecer Group Handicap

runners_data.name: Sioux Warrior
runners_data.note: Finished third on good ground over 6f most recently, showing this trip and surface are in his favour; Adrian Wintle's yard is 3/19 in 14 days and jockey Taryn Langley claims 5lb, which is a useful weight relief; runs in a hood and is the one hold-up horse whose recent sim-going figures offer the clearest comparable — 6 runs on similar ground with one win and four places.

runners_data.name: Ravenglass
runners_data.note: Has raced seven times on comparable going without winning, and his history is built over 7f rather than today's 6f, raising a genuine trip concern; as a true hold-up horse placed into a midfield slot by redistribution, he is likely to race out of his natural rhythm, and his STYLE_FIT of 0.93 signals that discount should apply to his chance in this shape.

runners_data.name: Reidh
runners_data.note: Tagged with a fade-in-finish flag and recent form reads 0-0-9-7 with double-figure placings consistently — on good-to-firm over 5f-7f the sim-going record is 10/15 with no wins or places, which is a significant red flag; Tom Queally's name lends ability to the saddle but the raw data here is hard to overcome and this horse is the most vulnerable in the field.

runners_data.name: Autumn Angel
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on soft ground 30 days ago and finished second on good ground over the same trip — the form is live and directly relevant; Tony Carroll's powerful 7/62 14-day strike rate keeps the stable warm, and Rowan Scott takes the ride; a natural hold-up horse displaced into midfield but the most in-form runner here, and one whose fitness and recent course-relevant distance profile makes her the chief threat regardless of positional constraints.

runners_data.name: Thanks Dad
runners_data.note: Recorded a zero on most recent run and has posted 8th, 10th, 10th, 13th, and 9th in recent outings — this is a horse in deep trouble for form; Tyler Heard takes the ride and the horse carries a visor, but there is no sim-going evidence of wins or places and redistribution into midfield compounds an already difficult profile.

runners_data.name: Marisitta
runners_data.note: All five recent runs have come over 7f-10f rather than today's 6f — this is a sharp distance drop and there is no recent evidence she handles the pace of a sprint; William Carson is a solid jockey booking but John O'Shea's 0/4 in 14 days is a quiet note, and being a hold-up horse pushed into a midfield slot when she may want to switch off late is a structural problem for her chance.

runners_data.name: Weston Court
runners_data.note: Five consecutive runs over 8f — today's 6f is the shortest trip he has faced in this sequence and that step down is unproven; Ronald Harris is 0/3 in the 14-day window and Ryan Kavanagh claims 5lb, which helps the weight; runs in blinkers and has some sim-going place form, but the combination of trip concern and redistribution out of his natural hold-up position makes this a speculative entry.

races.paceDynamic: This is a 6f handicap at Chepstow on good-to-firm ground where every single runner in the field carries a hold-up profile — there is no confirmed front-runner and no horse with a natural lead or prominent style to set the tempo. The race is almost certain to begin at a crawl as runners wait for rivals to commit, producing a compressed, tactical contest that converts into a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole. With the entire field defaulting to the rear, the winner will be the horse best placed on the rail or widest into the straight with the clearest run, and finishing speed over the final furlong is what separates them. This race shape heavily favours any horse who can position handily from a hold-up base when the field bunches, land a prominent berth without expending energy, and produce a sharp late kick — a strong finishing action on fast ground is the critical currency here. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than can all operate at the rear; Ravenglass, Autumn Angel, Weston Court, Marisitta, and Thanks Dad are all redistributed to midfield, meaning several will be forced to race closer than they want, and those who adapt most fluently to a handy midfield position are best placed to capitalise.

scenarios.body: If the pace is so negligible that the field virtually walks the first three furlongs and the race is settled by a single furlong of flat-out sprinting.

watchPoints.text: Autumn Angel is the form pick in the field — watch whether Rowan Scott allows her to drift naturally into a handy midfield position rather than being caught flat-footed at the rear; if she secures a clear run into the straight her recent 6f win and place make her the most dangerous finisher.

With no confirmed pace-setter among seven hold-up horses, watch the opening two furlongs for who instinctively quickens to fill the vacancy — any horse that slots into a lead-adjacent role uncontested will have a significant advantage in a race this slowly run.

Reidh's fade-in-finish tag combined with a sim-going record of 10/15 and no wins or places on comparable ground makes him a potential in-running danger to others if he drops out quickly and becomes an obstacle for closers seeking a run.

Draw and positioning at the top of the straight will be critical — Chepstow's flat 6f means the rail is not always fastest and horses with the widest, clearest passage in a bunched finish often have a decisive edge over those trapped on the inner seeking gaps.

Trainer Adrian Wintle saddles two runners (Sioux Warrior and Ravenglass) — watch in the early stages whether stable tactics emerge, with one horse potentially asked to settle closer to ensure the other gets a lead to aim at in the sprint finish.
